name: Bogø grid-connected wind conversion
description: A former direct-current wind plant was converted to supply alternating current to the SEAS grid.

impact.note: One converted plant showing wind could feed an alternating-current grid; its direct successor was the Gedser plant.

places.note: Place refers to the sourced event; historic political boundaries are not inferred.

date.basis: Date stated in the cited source.

events.statement: The converted Bogø wind plant began operating in autumn 1952 with an alternating-current grid connection.

evidence.supports: Juul describes the 1950 Vester Egesborg plant, 1952 Bogø conversion, and their contribution to Gedser design.

events.caveats: The source does not quantify customers, kWh or individual household access.

contributions.resource: Provided the alternating-current grid described by Juul
